english.title: Fail to take steps to ensure disclosed protected information is not further disclosed
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), having disclosed protected information, namely **(..SPECIFY INFORMATION..), in accordance with section 201(3) of the National Health Service Act 2006, failed to take all reasonable steps to ensure that, once disclosed by you, such information was not further disclosed to any person other than someone to whom it was necessary to disclose the information for a purpose connected with proceedings mentioned in section 202(1)(a) of the Act
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 202(2) and 205(1) and (2) of the National Health Service Act 2006.
english.pointstoprove:

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

other.penalty:
Summary: 51 weeks imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and/or a fine

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex - see legislation

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
